properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA-over-secp256k1 public-key recovery (ecrecover) shipped to on-chain programs: precompiles/src/secp256k1.rs (message digest is Keccak-256), SBF syscall sol_secp256k1_recover, vendored C implementation under programs/sbf/c/src/secp256k1_recover, libsecp256k1 0.7.2 dependency; remaining sites are cost tables, feature gates and fee counters governing the primitive at runtime. Consensus-critical: the curve is fixed by on-chain program semantics — changeable only via coordinated migration, not un

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All sampled sites compare PUBLIC on-chain values via ==: bank/blockhashes, genesis hashes, vote slot-hash pairs, shred/merkle signatures, gossip ping-pong echo tokens, default()/identity sentinels. No secret-dependent MAC or key comparison found on any page. Timing leakage is not exploitable for public values; retained as posture documentation — a constant-time compare is a cheap hardening if any site ever becomes secret-dependent.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile entry for the ECDSA-over-secp256k1 implementation (libsecp256k1/k256 family) that backs the ecrecover precompile and sol_secp256k1_recover syscall. Dependency inventory — the build ships this primitive whether or not this repo calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The chain's transaction and vote signature scheme: live batch-verify chains in core/src (sigverify.rs, bundle_sigverify_stage.rs, cluster_info_vote_listener.rs call solana_perf::sigverify::ed25519_verify*), ed25519 precompile with strict verification (SIMD-0152), ed25519-dalek 2.2 dependency, and cost/fee accounting. Consensus-critical — a move to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA requires a chain-wide signature migration; not changeable unilaterally.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two faces: (1) solana-curve25519 SBF syscalls shipped to on-chain zk programs — Edwards/Ristretto point ops and x25519 scalar multiplication, with compute-budget cost tables (compute-budget, program-runtime), feature gates, and dependency declarations; (2) the live TLS policy at tls-utils/src/crypto_provider.rs:8: rustls ring provider with kx_groups retained to X25519 ONLY, which governs every validator QUIC session (TPU ingress/egress, turbine, votor). Face (2) is harvest-now-decrypt-later rele

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA P-256 (secp256r1) verify precompile for on-chain programs (SIMD-0075), backed by vendored OpenSSL — precompiles/Cargo.toml enables the openssl-vendored feature and precompiles/src/secp256r1.rs:126 builds an openssl Verifier with SHA-256; sites include feature gates, fee counters (fee/src), cost constants and bench code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3 1.8.7 in live use: accounts-db per-account hashing, lattice-hash LtHash (consensus-relevant account-state hash), sol_blake3 SBF syscall (feature-gated, registered in syscalls/src/lib.rs:394-396), solana-blake3-hasher dependency, programs/sbf C headers. Hash — Grover square-root only, not Shor-broken; low urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 in live use: the sol_keccak256 SBF syscall (registered in syscalls/src/lib.rs:386) and the message-digest step of the secp256k1 ecrecover precompile (Ethereum-compatible), via solana-keccak-hasher 3.1.0; C headers under programs/sbf expose it to C programs. Hash — Grover square-root only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in live use: bundle hashing (bundle/src/lib.rs) and the digest step of the OpenSSL-backed secp256r1 verify precompile (precompiles/src/secp256r1.rs:126). SHA-256 is also the chain's core hash via external solana-hash/svm wrappers, and the sol_sha256 syscall registration (syscalls/src/lib.rs:383) has been reported as a separate finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac crate locked in the build — transitively reachable (e.g. jsonwebtoken HS256 used by the RPC auth path, whose verification-disabled site is another scout's object); no direct first-party call site observed in this repo. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 locked in the build as a transitive dependency; no direct first-party call site observed. Dependency inventory entry — notable because PBKDF2 parameters live inside the dependent crates, not here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3 package entry backing the live blake3 usage recorded under ALG-84de5a3e (accounts-db hashing, lattice-hash LtHash, sol_blake3 syscall). Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring is the process TLS provider: tls-utils/Cargo.toml enables rustls's "ring" feature and crypto_provider() instantiates rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider() for every validator QUIC session (TLS 1.3 suites, X25519-only kex after the retain filter, ed25519 inside the dummy x509 certs). Changeable here — switching to the aws-lc-rs provider with X25519MLKEM768 is a local change (the retain() must also be removed).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.23.45 — the TLS stack for all validator QUIC transport (quinn 0.11.12: TPU ingress server, TPU/turbine clients, votor transport) and the storage-bigtable gRPC channel. The local tls-utils crate pins the ring provider and strips kx groups to X25519, so no PQ group is offered even though modern rustls can negotiate X25519MLKEM768 with the aws-lc-rs provider. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 locked in the build — the SHA-256/SHA-512 implementations behind the external solana-hash/svm hashing wrappers, the sol_sha256/sol_sha512 syscalls, and Poh. Dependency inventory entry; live use sites are recorded under the SHA-256 object and syscall findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL in the lockfile — vendored OpenSSL backs the secp256r1 verify precompile (precompiles/Cargo.toml enables the "openssl-vendored" feature; openssl Verifier/EcGroup in precompiles/src/secp256r1.rs and its bench) and supplies platform TLS via native-tls for reqwest-based HTTP clients. Changeable here (the secp256r1 backend could move to pure-Rust p256/k256), but it is wired into a shipped precompile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Platform TLS (native-tls/OpenSSL) locked in for HTTP(S) client paths (reqwest in rpc-client and friends) — classical key exchange with no PQ option; the validator's own peer transport uses rustls over QUIC instead. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 in the locked build — and the protocol version of every validator QUIC session (quinn/rustls; "TLS 1.3-only config" in votor-transport/src/transport.rs; the rustls QUIC configs in streamer/quic-client/tpu-client-next). A good baseline; post-quantum readiness additionally requires hybrid kex groups, which tls-utils currently strips. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: k256 (pure-Rust secp256k1) locked in the build — transitive dependency for secp256k1 address/signature handling in sdk-level crates. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 crate locked in the build (transitive dependency); no direct first-party call site observed in this repo. Dependency inventory entry.
